capabilities.description: One Story and Acceptance Criterion identity moves from planning authority to repository authority.
capabilities.name: Lifecycle-aware authority

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must allow planning writers to create and revise only backlog Stories and their Acceptance Criteria.

stories.benefit: intent can mature without pretending it is accepted behavior
stories.goal: refine Stories and Acceptance Criteria while they remain in the backlog
stories.title: Shape behavior before implementation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must preserve matching planning Story and Acceptance Criterion identities when a repository contract is synchronized.

scenarios.given: planning changes after a materializing branch was created
scenarios.then: Tieline must project the merged definition and preserve the later planning revision as a handoff conflict
scenarios.when: the reviewed repository definition is synchronized

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must keep read, planning-write, repository-sync, and offline-admin database responsibilities separate.
Tieline must remove projected code assets that the synchronized repository contract no longer declares and that no contract record still links.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Postgres is a projection of the repository manifest, so a renamed path or a reworded selector otherwise strands a code asset that holds a frozen content hash and still answers the artifact overlap lookup, and the projection drifts further with every rename until it is rebuilt from scratch.

scenarios.given: a synchronized repository contract whose linked implementation path was renamed
scenarios.then: the code asset for the former path must be removed, while an asset owned by another repository or still linked by another contract record must be retained
scenarios.when: the repository contract is synchronized again

stories.benefit: stable identity survives delivery without two writers
stories.goal: materialize planning definitions with the implementation
stories.title: Transfer accepted behavior to repository authority

capabilities.description: Accepted product behavior is strict, reviewable, and measurable beside the implementation.
capabilities.name: Living product contract

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must reject repository contract documents that violate the accepted Story and Acceptance Criterion schema.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Structural failures make semantic impact and synchronization untrustworthy.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must compile deterministic manifests and report direct-AC and repository mapping coverage with explicit gaps.

scenarios.given: ten eligible source files and eight mapped paths
scenarios.then: Tieline must report 80 percent coverage and name both unmapped files
scenarios.when: mapping coverage is calculated

scenarios.given: configured source roots contain no eligible files
scenarios.then: Tieline must report that coverage is not measured instead of reporting 100 percent
scenarios.when: mapping coverage is calculated

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report affected Acceptance Criteria and freshness for changed, renamed, or deleted linked paths without blocking on semantic findings.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Drift should be visible during review while the MVP remains warn-only.

scenarios.given: a linked implementation path changes without a refreshed manifest
scenarios.then: Tieline must report the linked criterion as impacted and stale
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must render accepted Stories and Acceptance Criteria as a self-contained human-readable review page.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Maintainers outside the implementation can review the same repository-owned contract accepted by the pull request.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must exit non-zero when the check runs in strict mode and the committed manifest does not match the compiled manifest.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: An agent-managed contract needs a machine-checkable gate because no human verifies the warn-only output, so a stale manifest merges unnoticed unless the command fails.

scenarios.given: the committed manifest does not match the compiled manifest
scenarios.then: Tieline must exit non-zero and name the stale manifest
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base in strict mode

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The check report must label affected Acceptance Criteria as impact rather than as warnings, and must reserve warnings for findings that require an action.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Impacts answer which behavior a change touches, which is orientation rather than a defect. Labelling orientation as a warning trains every reader to skip the stream, so the warnings that do require an action stop being read.

scenarios.given: a change modifies linked paths while the committed manifest is stale
scenarios.then: affected Acceptance Criteria must be reported as impact and exactly one warning must name the stale manifest
scenarios.when: the branch is checked against its base

stories.benefit: intent and implementation change through the same review
stories.goal: define product behavior in a stable Story and Acceptance Criterion hierarchy
stories.title: Review accepted behavior with code

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report every acceptance criterion that links a repository-relative path, must distinguish a link carried by the acceptance criterion itself from one carried only by its Story, and must state explicitly when no acceptance criterion governs the path.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Coverage answers for the whole contract and check answers for a diff, so both describe a violation that already exists; the pre-change question is the only one that can prevent it. An empty array reads to an agent like a failed query rather than the finding that the code is ungoverned.

scenarios.given: a path is linked by one acceptance criterion and by the Story that owns it
scenarios.then: Tieline must return both records and mark them direct and story_fallback
scenarios.when: the governing criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a path exists in the repository and no contract link targets it
scenarios.then: Tieline must state that no acceptance criterion governs it instead of returning an empty result
scenarios.when: the governing criteria for that path are requested

scenarios.given: a requested path does not exist in the repository
scenarios.then: Tieline must report it distinctly from a path that exists but is ungoverned
scenarios.when: the governing criteria for that path are requested

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The governing-criteria lookup must answer from the compiled manifest alone, so Tieline must serve it over MCP with no database connection and must return a named, actionable message when no workspace or no readable manifest is found.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Every other MCP tool fails at call time without Postgres, so an offline server boots and answers nothing; a manifest-backed lookup is what makes serving without a database worth doing, and an obscure throw would waste the one answer the caller came for.

scenarios.given: no database connection is configured
scenarios.then: Tieline must return the governing acceptance criteria and the commit the manifest records
scenarios.when: the governing criteria for a path are requested over MCP

scenarios.given: the server runs outside any Tieline workspace
scenarios.then: Tieline must name the missing workspace and the command that creates one
scenarios.when: the governing criteria for a path are requested

stories.benefit: a contradiction with accepted behavior is prevented instead of reported afterwards
stories.goal: resolve a repository path to the accepted behavior that already governs it
stories.title: Learn which acceptance criteria govern a path before editing it

capabilities.description: Requests, bugs, questions, optional work, and help content remain distinct from accepted behavior.
capabilities.name: Evidence and planning intake

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must append an Observation before semantic matching and allow it to remain unattributed.

scenarios.given: semantic matching fails after intake
scenarios.then: Tieline must return the stored record for a later matching retry
scenarios.when: an Observation has already been stored

stories.benefit: source evidence is never lost or forced into an incorrect feature
stories.goal: record a request, bug, or question without first finding a product definition
stories.title: Preserve source observations before attribution

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must let a Backlog Item target zero or more Stories and Acceptance Criteria without becoming their lifecycle container.

stories.benefit: planning work remains separate from the product contract
stories.goal: group evidence and target existing or future behavior
stories.title: Consolidate optional work without duplicating behavior

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must resolve help content by source and external identifier while preserving Story and Acceptance Criterion backlinks.

stories.benefit: accepted behavior can point to documentation maintained elsewhere
stories.goal: ingest and retrieve help content by its source identity
stories.title: Connect external help without copying its identity

capabilities.description: Contract links carry judged, fenced evidence instead of an unchecked claim that a path relates to an Acceptance Criterion.
capabilities.name: Graded link evidence

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must emit a grading scope limited to the contract links impacted by the diff against a base ref, and every scope entry must carry its Acceptance Criterion text, relation, artifact path, and extracted symbol vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Grading every link costs far more than the signal is worth, and the diff already identifies which claims changed.

scenarios.given: a branch changes one linked implementation file
scenarios.then: Tieline must emit exactly the Acceptance Criterion and path pair for that file
scenarios.when: the grading scope is emitted against the base ref

scenarios.given: a branch changes a file that no Acceptance Criterion links
scenarios.then: Tieline must emit an empty scope
scenarios.when: the grading scope is emitted against the base ref

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must build the citable symbol vocabulary of an artifact from its declarations alone, so an identifier that appears only inside a comment or a string literal must not be citable.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Substring presence would let a symbol named only in prose satisfy a supported grade, which is the confirmation the fence exists to refuse.

scenarios.given: an artifact names an identifier only inside a comment
scenarios.then: Tieline must exclude that identifier from the vocabulary
scenarios.when: its symbol vocabulary is extracted

scenarios.given: an artifact is missing, empty, or not a TypeScript source
scenarios.then: Tieline must return an empty vocabulary instead of failing the run
scenarios.when: its symbol vocabulary is extracted

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Grading must remain a pure function of the compiled manifest, the working tree, and the git diff, so Tieline must never require a database, a network call, or a model credential to grade a link.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Validate, compile, coverage, and check all run with zero infrastructure; a grading command that needed a credential would break the property that makes the offline plane adoptable.

stories.benefit: a link claim can be judged instead of assumed
stories.goal: learn which contract links a change touches and which symbols may be cited as evidence for them
stories.title: Grade the links a change touches

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must downgrade a supported grade to unsupported and report the downgrade whenever the cited symbol is absent from the extracted vocabulary for that artifact.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Grade quality varies with whichever host model runs the skill, so the fence has to make a false confirmation structurally unreachable rather than merely unlikely.

scenarios.given: a verdict grades a link supported and cites a symbol the artifact never declares
scenarios.then: Tieline must record the link as unsupported and name the fabricated citation in its report
scenarios.when: the submitted verdicts are verified

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A scoped link that receives no submitted verdict must be reported as unsupported rather than skipped.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A skill that dies halfway, or a grader that quietly avoids a hard link, must not read as success; absence is the refusal path, not a gap.

scenarios.given: a grading scope contains a link that no submitted verdict names
scenarios.then: Tieline must report that link as unsupported and state that no verdict was submitted
scenarios.when: the submitted verdicts are verified

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Grade verification must exit non-zero only when strict mode is requested while an unsupported grade remains, and must otherwise exit zero while still printing every unsupported grade.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Gating on model-mediated judgment before its false-positive rate is known would poison trust in the tool, so grading stays advisory until that rate is observed.

scenarios.given: verification leaves an unsupported grade and strict mode is not requested
scenarios.then: Tieline must print the unsupported grade and exit zero
scenarios.when: the command finishes

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The grading skill must direct the host agent to cite only symbols from the emitted vocabulary, to print every grade before verification, and to treat unsupported as an expected outcome.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The judgment step is the one part of the pipeline Tieline cannot check, so the instructions that constrain it are part of the shipped behavior.

stories.benefit: a false confirmation cannot reach merge unnoticed
stories.goal: see every refused and downgraded grade rather than a silent pass
stories.title: Refuse evidence claims that cannot be checked

capabilities.description: Focused semantic documents and auditable suggestions help equivalent language converge.
capabilities.name: Semantic matching and consolidation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must derive separate semantic documents for Stories, Acceptance Criteria, Scenarios, Backlog Items, and sanitized Observations.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Focused documents preserve specificity and avoid re-embedding unrelated criteria.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must apply retrieval metadata as narrowing filters before combining always-on full-text and identifier recall with optional vector, alias, artifact-overlap, and three-hop graph signals through reciprocal rank fusion.

scenarios.given: a caller supplies an Observation anchor with only a dismissed relationship to an Acceptance Criterion
scenarios.then: the dismissed relationship must contribute no graph proximity
scenarios.when: Tieline ranks the authorized semantic candidate set

scenarios.given: no embedding provider is installed or reachable
scenarios.then: Tieline must return full-text or identifier matches with explicit signal features and match reasons
scenarios.when: a caller searches with an authorized retrieval profile

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must keep similarity-only relationships suggested until an explicit decision confirms or dismisses them.

scenarios.given: a high-scoring semantic match without an explicit human decision
scenarios.then: its state must remain suggested
scenarios.when: the suggestion is persisted

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must withhold a semantic candidate whose vector, lexical, and alias signals all fall below an absolute magnitude floor, even when its blended rank-fusion score clears the presentation cutoff.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The blended score is mostly reciprocal rank fusion, which measures a candidate's position inside the returned set rather than how well it matches, so the best member of a weak set scores almost exactly what the best member of a strong set scores. Only a floor on the raw comparable signals stops the least wrong available option from reading as a good match to a caller acting without human review.

scenarios.given: the only retrieved candidate carries 0.30 vector similarity and 0.20 lexical similarity
scenarios.then: the candidate must be withheld even though its blended score clears the presentation cutoff
scenarios.when: Tieline assembles Observation match candidates or planning-create advice

scenarios.given: a candidate matches a recorded alias exactly but carries low vector and lexical similarity
scenarios.then: the candidate must be retained because an exact alias match is a deterministic identifier match rather than a fuzzy one
scenarios.when: Tieline applies the magnitude floor

stories.benefit: alternate phrasing converges without deleting source history
stories.goal: find equivalent Stories, Acceptance Criteria, work, and evidence
stories.title: Search before creating product or planning records

capabilities.description: Callers retrieve exact or semantic business context without confusing production truth and planning material.
capabilities.name: Intent-aware organization search

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must return structured Stories with ordered Acceptance Criteria, direct and fallback links, coverage, freshness, lifecycle, and authority.

stories.benefit: answers stay grounded in the most specific known contract
stories.goal: inspect behavior with its evidence and state
stories.title: Retrieve Stories through their Acceptance Criteria

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must resolve a versioned retrieval profile before cross-type search and allow caller filters only to narrow it.

scenarios.given: the support profile excludes planning authority
scenarios.then: Tieline must search only the repository intersection
scenarios.when: a caller requests both planning and repository authority

stories.benefit: the result state is clear without permanently hiding useful records
stories.goal: choose production, engineering, discovery, or full authorized context
stories.title: Select an explicit retrieval intent

capabilities.description: Tieline initializes, serves, and composes its contract capabilities without leaking privileged writers into read paths.
capabilities.name: Portable and safe operation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must keep shared repository configuration portable while storing clone-local setup state and database credentials in a private external profile.
Tieline must report workspace initialization, clone-local setup, and database-backed capability configuration as separate states.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: A tracked config cannot prove that another clone has credentials or semantic matching available.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must surface detected source roots and preflight warnings while leaving the specification empty until repository-specific semantic onboarding.

stories.benefit: the repository remains shareable without committing secrets
stories.goal: configure contract roots and private runtime credentials
stories.title: Initialize a portable Tieline workspace

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must compose read, evidence-write, and planning-write capabilities without exposing repository synchronization through MCP tools.
Tieline must serve stdio by default and require explicit gateway configuration for non-loopback HTTP.
Tieline must provide a loud in-memory test seam for contract and tool verification without weakening production adapters.
Tieline must expose a semantic-authoring prompt that uses configured repository context and falls back to disclosed local duplicate checks when database-backed matching is unavailable.

stories.benefit: tool capabilities match their database authority
stories.goal: use a focused contract, search, evidence, and planning interface
stories.title: Serve lifecycle-aware tools through MCP

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must run the clean lifecycle integration suite against a disposable baseline database.

stories.benefit: clean installations prove the shared contract end to end
stories.goal: exercise evidence, planning, authority transfer, profiles, and the baseline together
stories.title: Verify the lifecycle as one system
